overview.purpose: A RESTful bookstore API built with Node.js and Express. Provides CRUD operations for books, authors, and orders. Uses PostgreSQL for persistence and Redis for caching popular book queries.
setupSteps: cp .env.example .env — fill in DB_URL and REDIS_URL

modules.name: API Layer
modules.summary: Express router configuration, middleware pipeline, and request/response lifecycle. All HTTP endpoints are defined here, including versioning under /api/v1. Auth middleware is applied per-router, not per-route.

quiz.question: Where is authentication middleware applied in the API layer?
options: Per individual route handler using a decorator pattern
Per-router in the route file, applied to all routes in that group
Globally in app.js before all route registration
In the database layer as a query interceptor
quiz.explanation: Auth middleware is applied per-router — meaning every route in a given file inherits it. This is set in each route file (e.g. books.js uses router.use(auth)), not per individual handler or globally.

quiz.question: What is the base path prefix for all API endpoints?
quiz.explanation: All routes are versioned under /api/v1. This allows future breaking changes to be introduced under /api/v2 without disrupting existing clients.

quiz.question: Which file is the Express application entry point (not the HTTP server)?
quiz.explanation: src/app.js creates and configures the Express app — middleware, routes, error handler. src/server.js simply imports the app and calls app.listen(). Separating them makes testing easier.

quiz.question: How are unhandled errors surfaced to the client?
options: Each route handler has its own try/catch that sends a 500
Express default error handler formats them as HTML
A central errorHandler middleware formats all thrown errors as JSON
Errors crash the process and are restarted by a process manager
quiz.explanation: src/middleware/errorHandler.js is registered last in app.js. Any error passed to next(err) — including async throws — flows here and is formatted as a consistent JSON error response.

explainBack.prompt: In your own words, explain how an incoming HTTP request flows through this codebase from the moment it arrives until a response is sent. Be specific about what each middleware does and in what order.

rubric.concept: Request enters app.js and passes through global middleware (CORS, body parser, logging)
Router selects the correct route file based on path prefix (/api/v1/books etc)
Auth middleware validates the JWT token before any route handler runs
Route handler processes the request, calls service/data layer, sends response
Errors passed to next(err) are caught by errorHandler and formatted as JSON

sabotage.symptom: All API requests return 200 OK regardless of whether a valid JWT token is provided. Even requests with no Authorization header succeed.
sabotage.injectedDiff:
-  if (!token) return next(createError(401, 'No token provided'));
+  if (!token) return next();
hints: The symptom affects all routes equally — focus on code that runs before every handler.
Look at the auth middleware function. Trace what happens when the Authorization header is missing.
Line 14 of src/middleware/auth.js — the early return on missing token has been modified.

quests.title: Add request ID header to all responses
quests.rationale: Low-blast-radius addition. Creates a new middleware file and registers it in app.js. Teaches the middleware registration pattern without touching existing logic.

quests.title: Fix outdated authentication docs
quests.rationale: README claims auth uses session cookies but the code uses JWT Bearer tokens. Safe first contribution — docs only, no code change.

modules.name: Data Layer
modules.summary: PostgreSQL access via pg-promise. All queries are in typed repository classes — BookRepository, AuthorRepository, OrderRepository. Redis is used as a read-through cache for the books list endpoint with a 60-second TTL.

quiz.question: How long does the Redis cache store the book list before expiring?
quiz.explanation: The Redis TTL is set to 60 seconds in src/cache/redis.js. This means the book list may be up to 60 seconds stale after a write. Cache is invalidated explicitly on write operations.

quiz.question: What library is used for PostgreSQL queries?
quiz.explanation: pg-promise wraps node-postgres and adds promise support, parameterized queries, and transaction helpers. Repository classes use the db instance from src/db/index.js.

quiz.question: Which module is most dangerous to modify without understanding its blast radius?
quiz.explanation: src/db/index.js creates the single shared database connection pool used by all three repositories. Changing it affects every data operation in the system — the highest blast radius of any file in this layer.

quiz.question: What pattern do the repository classes follow for write operations with respect to caching?
options: Write to cache first, then async write to DB
Write to DB, then explicitly invalidate the relevant cache key
Write to DB only; cache expires naturally via TTL
All writes bypass both cache and DB and use an event queue
quiz.explanation: Repository write methods (create, update, delete) write to PostgreSQL first, then call the Redis client to delete the affected cache key. This ensures consistency at the cost of one extra cache miss after each write.

explainBack.prompt: Describe how a GET /api/v1/books request retrieves data. Walk through the cache check, what happens on a hit vs a miss, and what the repository does when talking to the database.

rubric.concept: Request hits the route handler which calls BookRepository.findAll()
Repository checks Redis for a cached result before querying PostgreSQL
On cache hit: returns cached JSON directly without touching the DB
On cache miss: queries PostgreSQL, stores result in Redis with 60s TTL, returns result

sabotage.symptom: POST /api/v1/orders returns 200 and a valid order object, but the order never appears in subsequent GET requests. The database shows no new rows after a POST.
sabotage.correctOriginal: await db.tx(async t => { await t.none(insertQuery, values); });
hints: The order is created in memory but not persisted. Focus on the write path in OrderRepository.
Look at how the transaction is committed in OrderRepository.create(). Is the commit actually awaited?
Line 34 — the transaction wrapper is present but the await before the commit call was removed.

quests.title: Add index on orders.created_at column
quests.rationale: New migration file only — no changes to existing migrations or repository code. Good first exposure to the migration pattern.

modules.name: Test Suite
modules.summary: Jest test suite with unit tests for repositories (using pg-mem as an in-memory PostgreSQL) and integration tests for API routes using supertest. Test coverage sits at 67% — the orders route is notably undertested.

quiz.question: What library is used to simulate PostgreSQL in unit tests?
options: A real test database running in Docker
Mock functions only — no DB simulation
quiz.explanation: pg-mem provides an in-memory implementation of the PostgreSQL wire protocol. Unit tests use it via tests/helpers/dbSetup.js, which sets up a fresh database before each test.

quiz.question: Which part of the system is most undertested according to the coverage report?
quiz.explanation: The module summary flags orders as notably undertested. tests/integration/orders.test.js exists but covers only the happy path — no tests for invalid payloads, missing auth, or transaction failures.

quiz.question: What library is used for HTTP integration tests?
quiz.explanation: supertest wraps the Express app and makes HTTP requests without starting a real server on a port. Tests import the app directly, making them fast and self-contained.

explainBack.prompt: Explain how the test suite is structured. How do unit tests differ from integration tests here, and what is the known gap in coverage you would prioritize fixing first?

rubric.concept: Unit tests use pg-mem to simulate PostgreSQL without a real DB connection
Integration tests use supertest to make HTTP requests against the Express app directly
The orders route is undertested — only happy path is covered
dbSetup.js provides a shared test database helper to keep setup DRY

quests.title: Add test for missing auth token on POST /orders
quests.rationale: Adds one test case to an existing file. No new files, no new patterns. Directly addresses the known coverage gap and is isolated to the test suite.

quests.title: Fix misleading test coverage badge in README
quests.rationale: README shows 85% coverage badge but actual coverage is 67%. Safe documentation fix with real impact on team trust in the test suite.

diagrams.title: System Architecture
diagrams.mermaid:
graph TD
  Client([HTTP Client]) --> App[src/app.js]
  App --> AuthMW[auth middleware]
  AuthMW --> Books[/api/v1/books]
  AuthMW --> Authors[/api/v1/authors]
  AuthMW --> Orders[/api/v1/orders]
  Books --> BookRepo[BookRepository]
  Authors --> AuthorRepo[AuthorRepository]
  Orders --> OrderRepo[OrderRepository]
  BookRepo --> Redis[(Redis Cache)]
  BookRepo --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
  AuthorRepo --> PG
  OrderRepo --> PG
  Redis -.->|cache miss| PG

diagrams.title: GET /books — Cache Flow
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant R as Router
  participant BR as BookRepository
  participant Redis
  participant PG as PostgreSQL
  C->>R: GET /api/v1/books
  R->>BR: findAll()
  BR->>Redis: GET books:list
  alt Cache Hit
    Redis-->>BR: cached JSON
    BR-->>R: books array
  else Cache Miss
    Redis-->>BR: null
    BR->>PG: SELECT * FROM books
    PG-->>BR: rows
    BR->>Redis: SET books:list (TTL 60s)
    BR-->>R: books array
  end
  R-->>C: 200 { data: [...] }

```
Authorization: Bearer <your-jwt-token>
```

Tokens are issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login and expire after 24 hours.

glossary.definition: A PostgreSQL adapter for Node.js that wraps node-postgres with promise support, parameterized queries, and transaction helpers.
An abstraction layer that encapsulates all database queries for a given entity type. In this codebase, BookRepository, AuthorRepository, and OrderRepository each own their entity's data access.
An in-memory PostgreSQL implementation used in unit tests to avoid a real database dependency.
A caching strategy where the cache layer sits between the application and the database. On a cache miss, data is fetched from the DB and stored in cache before returning to the caller.

dangerZones.reason: Creates the single shared database connection pool. All repository classes depend on this instance — changes here affect every data operation.
Applied to all protected routes. A regression here disables or bypasses authentication globally.
